questions.key_step: Recognise C = |A| I (cofactor expansion / alien cofactors), then evaluate |A| with log base changes
questions.justification: Short but chains three routine moves: cofactor identity, change of base, |C| = |A|^2; options available.

questions.key_step: a3a5 = a4^2 and a2+a4 give the ratio, then the three-term sum
questions.justification: Routine GP chain; a few steps but no insight and options to check.

questions.key_step: Take terms a-d, a, a+d, bound S20 and pick the integer common difference
questions.justification: Standard AP with an inequality and an integrality condition; two stages.

questions.key_step: adj(A) is unipotent so its powers are [[1,-2k],[0,1]]; add the geometric-like series
questions.justification: Routine once the pattern of powers is seen; short chain.

questions.key_step: Sum and product of roots give a and b, then form the new equation
questions.justification: One familiar move (sum/product of roots) applied twice; fully routine.

questions.key_step: Entries are rank-one (sqrt2)^i (sqrt2)^j, so A^2 = 14A, or multiply out directly
questions.justification: Direct 3x3 multiplication with surds; routine, slip risk only.

questions.key_step: 4 + 3r^2 + r^4 = (r^2+2)^2 - r^2 factors the denominator and makes the sum telescope
questions.justification: Idea of completing the square to factor the denominator is not immediately visible; then a telescoping sum.

questions.key_step: BCB^-1 = A makes C = B^-1AB, so C^2 = B, C^4 = B^2; then compare entries of B^2 + aB + bI = O
questions.justification: Two linked ideas (similarity powers and AB^-1 = A^-1 giving A^2 = B) then matrix equation.

questions.key_step: r^4 - 3r^2 + 1 = (r^2-r-1)(r^2+r-1) and r is half the difference of the factors
questions.justification: Same hidden telescoping as Q7; the factorisation must be found.

questions.key_step: Sum and product of roots with the GP ratio fix R = 4/3, then (a-b)^2
questions.justification: Routine multi-step use of Vieta with a GP substitution.

questions.key_step: R1-R2, R2-R3 expand to the required sum, or write M = D + 1 w^T
questions.justification: Needs a manipulation that is not mechanical; a poor choice makes it long.

questions.key_step: Differences of sums give nd and (2n-1)d, then solve for n and d
questions.justification: Routine AP chain, small algebra.

questions.key_step: Discriminant < 0 gives a in (-19,5); sum of squares of integers
questions.justification: Two routine stages with a sum-of-squares formula.

questions.key_step: Power-sum recurrence P_n + sqrt3 P_{n-1} - 16 P_{n-2} = 0 from the root equation
questions.justification: One recurrence used twice; options help.

questions.key_step: Put x = 0 to get lambda, then form the equation with roots lambda and lambda/3
questions.justification: Routine determinant evaluation and Vieta.

questions.key_step: |adj(kA)| = k^{n(n-1)}|A|^{n-1} type identities, then compare powers of 2 and 3
questions.justification: Property chain with an easy trap (which scalar multiplies A).

questions.key_step: Differences give nd and (2n-1)d; solve for n
questions.justification: Routine AP system.

questions.key_step: Second differences are constant, so T_n is quadratic; sum with standard sums
questions.justification: Standard difference method, routine summation.

questions.key_step: det(P^-1AP - 2I) = det(A - 2I)
questions.justification: One familiar similarity trick, then a 3x3 determinant and factorisation.

questions.key_step: adj properties and N = -M^T (odd order) give |M|^4 = 2^8, then solve for alpha
questions.justification: Several determinant identities chained, with a sign and a positivity condition on alpha.
